title: Design a Search Autocomplete System
summary: Design a real-time search autocomplete/typeahead system.
body:
Design a real-time search autocomplete/typeahead system.

## Scenario

Design a typeahead suggestion system that shows top search suggestions as users type, similar to Google Search autocomplete.

## Requirements

- Return top 5 suggestions within 100ms of each keystroke
- Rank suggestions by popularity/relevance
- Support personalized suggestions based on user history
- Handle 10K queries per second
- Update suggestion rankings as search trends change

## Constraints

- Response time < 100ms at p99
- Suggestions must be safe (no offensive content)
- Support multiple languages
- Graceful degradation under load

## What a strong answer covers

- Trie vs inverted index for prefix matching
- Ranking algorithm (frequency, recency, personalization)
- Data collection and aggregation pipeline
- Caching strategy for popular prefixes
- Real-time vs batch index updates

## Reference walkthrough

Trie data structure with frequency counts at each node. Top-K results cached at each prefix node. Two-tier architecture: real-time trie in Redis for hot queries, batch-rebuilt trie from Hadoop/Spark for comprehensive coverage. Zookeeper for trie version management across replicas. Sampling collector aggregates search queries into frequency counts hourly. Content filter service screens suggestions before indexing. Client-side debounce (200ms) + browser caching of recent prefixes.
keyTakeaways: Trie vs inverted index for prefix matching
